questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). In February 1905 at London, Shaymji Krishna Verma estab- lished the Indian Home Rule Society, which is also known as ‘India House.’ The aim of this society was to establish self-rule by intimidating the British Government. From here, a newspaper ‘The Indian Sociologist’ was started. Shyamji departed from London for Paris due to over activeness of Government machinery and later to Geneva.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) फरवरी 1905 में लंदन में श्यामजी कृष्ण वर्मा ने इंडियन होम रूल सोसाइटी की स्थापना की, जिसे 'इंडिया हाउस' के नाम से भी जाना जाता है। इस सोसाइटी का उद्देश्य ब्रिटिश सरकार को डराकर स्वशासन स्थापित करना था। यहीं से एक समाचार पत्र 'द इंडियन सोशियोलॉजिस्ट' प्रारंभ हुआ। सरकारी मशीनरी की अत्यधिक सक्रियता के कारण श्यामजी लंदन से पेरिस और बाद में जिनेवा के लिए प्रस्थान कर गये।

questions.questionTextEn: Who among the following founded the ‘Ghadar Party’?
questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से किसने 'गदर पार्टी' की स्थापना की?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). In 1913 at San Francisco, Sohan Singh Bhakna founded "Hindustani workers of the Paciﬁ c Coast" organization. This organization published a newspaper 'Gadar,' that is why this organization was later known as the Ghadar Party. Lala Har- dayal was also one of its founder members and torchbearer. Other members of ‘Gadar Party’ were Raja Mahendra Pratap, Abdul Rahman, Madam Bhikaji Kama, Bhai Parmanand, Kartar Singh Sarabha and Pandit Kashiram. Since in the option Sohan Singh Bhakana’s name is not given therefore option ‘a’ is correct.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) 1913 में सैन फ्रांसिस्को में सोहन सिंह भकना ने "हिन्दुस्तानी वर्कर्स ऑफ द पैसिफिक कोस्ट" संगठन की स्थापना की। इस संगठन ने एक समाचार पत्र 'गदर' प्रकाशित किया, इसीलिए इस संगठन को बाद में गदर पार्टी के नाम से जाना गया। लाला हरदयाल भी इसके संस्थापक सदस्यों और पथप्रदर्शक में से एक थे। 'गदर पार्टी' के अन्य सदस्य राजा महेंद्र प्रताप, अब्दुल रहमान, मैडम भीकाजी कामा, भाई परमानंद, करतार सिंह सराभा और पंडित काशीराम थे। चूँकि विकल्प में सोहन सिंह भकाणा का नाम नहीं दिया गया है इसलिए विकल्प 'ए' सही है।

questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन ग़दर पार्टी के पहले अध्यक्ष थे?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). The Ghadar Party was an organization founded by expatriate Indians settled in the United States and Canada in 1913 with the aim of securing India’s independence from British rule. Key members included Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha, and Rasbihari Bose. Sohan Singh Bhakna was the ﬁ rst Chairman of the Gadar Party. The party used to publish ‘Ghadar’ newspaper which was published in Urdu, Punjabi, Gujrati, Hindi etc. language.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) ग़दर पार्टी 1913 में संयुक्त राज्य अमेरिका और कनाडा में बसे प्रवासी भारतीयों द्वारा ब्रिटिश शासन से भारत की आजादी हासिल करने के उद्देश्य से स्थापित एक संगठन था। प्रमुख सदस्यों में लाला हरदयाल, सोहन सिंह भकना, करतार सिंह सराभा और रासबिहारी बोस शामिल थे। सोहन सिंह भकना गदर पार्टी के पहले अध्यक्ष थे। पार्टी 'ग़दर' अखबार निकालती थी जो उर्दू, पंजाबी, गुजराती, हिंदी आदि भाषाओं में प्रकाशित होता था।

questions.questionTextHi: निम्नलिखित में से किसने विदेश में रिपब्लिकन सरकार की स्थापना की?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). During the World War-I, Raja Mahendra Pratap established the ﬁ rst provisional Government of India at Kabul in Af- ghanistan in 1915. In this Government Raja Mahendra Pratap himself became President, and his associate Maulavi Barkatullah worked as Prime Minister. Germany and Russia gave recognition to this Government.

questions.questionTextEn: Who is regarded as the “Mother of Indian Revolu- tion”:
questions.questionTextHi: "भारतीय क्रांति की जननी" किसे माना जाता है:
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (D). Bhikaji Cama was an Indian freedom ﬁ ghter and political activist. She was born to an extremely wealthy Parsi business family. She led the revolutionary movement from America and Europe for India’s freedom. At the International Socialist Congress held at Stuttgart (Germany) in 1907, she was the ﬁ rst person to hoist Indian Flag on foreign land. She struggled with her full strength for Indian freedom and worked for it residing in Paris. In 1935 she returned to Mumbai and in August, 1936 she died. She was popularly known as ‘’Mother of Indian Revolution’’.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (D) भीकाजी कामा एक भारतीय स्वतंत्रता सेनानी और राजनीतिक कार्यकर्ता थीं। उनका जन्म एक अत्यंत धनी पारसी व्यवसायी परिवार में हुआ था। उन्होंने भारत की आज़ादी के लिए अमेरिका और यूरोप से क्रांतिकारी आंदोलन का नेतृत्व किया। 1907 में स्टटगार्ट (जर्मनी) में आयोजित अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सोशलिस्ट कांग्रेस में, वह विदेशी भूमि पर भारतीय ध्वज फहराने वाली पहली व्यक्ति थीं। उन्होंने भारतीय स्वतंत्रता के लिए अपनी पूरी ताकत से संघर्ष किया और पेरिस में रहकर इसके लिए काम किया। 1935 में वह मुंबई लौट आईं और अगस्त, 1936 में उनकी मृत्यु हो गई। वह ''भारतीय क्रांति की जननी'' के नाम से लोकप्रिय थीं।

questions.questionTextEn: Consider the following statements about Madam Bhi- kaji Cama: 1. Madam Cama unfurled the National Flag at the International Socialist Conference in Paris in the year 1907. 2. Madam Cama served as private secretary to Dada- bhai Naoroji. 3. Madam Cama was born to Parsi. Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi: मैडम भीकाजी कामा के बारे में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें: 1. मैडम कामा ने वर्ष 1907 में पेरिस में अंतर्राष्ट्रीय समाजवादी सम्मेलन में राष्ट्रीय ध्वज फहराया। 2. मैडम कामा ने दादा-भाई नौरोजी के निजी सचिव के रूप में कार्य किया। 3. मैडम कामा का जन्म पारसी से हुआ था। ऊपर दिए गए कथनों में से कौन सा/से सही है/हैं?
questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (B). Madam Bhikaji Cama was born on 24th September, 1861. Her parents were Parsi. Sorabji Patel was her father. She was married to Rustan K.R Cama. He was an advocate and social activist. Madam Cama worked as a personal secretary of Dada Bhai Naoroji, the great leader of Indian National Movement. After some period she associated herself with the Freedom Movement when she came into the contact of Europian scholars and students. (For rest of the details about Madam Cama, please see the above question). She ﬁ rst unfurled the National Flag at International Socialist Congress on 22nd August, 1907 in Germany’s Stuttgart.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (B) मैडम भीकाजी कामा का जन्म 24 सितंबर, 1861 को हुआ था। उनके माता-पिता पारसी थे। सोराबजी पटेल उनके पिता थे। उनका विवाह रुस्टन के.आर कामा से हुआ था। वह एक वकील और सामाजिक कार्यकर्ता थे। मैडम कामा ने भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के महान नेता दादा भाई नौरोजी के निजी सचिव के रूप में काम किया। कुछ समय बाद जब वह यूरोपीय विद्वानों और छात्रों के संपर्क में आईं तो उन्होंने खुद को स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन से जोड़ लिया। (मैडम कामा के बारे में बाकी जानकारी के लिए कृपया उपरोक्त प्रश्न देखें)। उन्होंने पहली बार 22 अगस्त, 1907 को जर्मनी के स्टटगार्ट में अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सोशलिस्ट कांग्रेस में राष्ट्रीय ध्वज फहराया।

questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). The Kamagatamaru was a Japanese steamliner chartered by an afﬂ uent Punjabi businessman, Gurdit Singh to bring In- dian immigrants to Canada. The ship departed in 1914, taking 376 Indians for Canada’s Vancouver port, but the Canadian police refused their entry in Canada. A Shore Committee was constituted to protect the rights of Indian travellers under the leadership of Hussain Rahim, Balwant Singh, and Sohan Lal Pathak. Indian, Bhagwan Singh, Barkatullah, Ramchand and Sohan Singh also carried out a movement in favour of Indian emigrants. When Kamagatamaru reached Budge Budge port at Calcutta, a clash occurred between angered passengers and British Police. In ﬁ ring by the Police, 20 of the passenger were killed, one drowned and 202 passengers were sent to Jail.

questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (A). The Ghadar Movement was an early 20th century, international political movement organised by expatriate Indians to overthrow British rule in India. The ofﬁ cial date for the birth of the movement has been considered a meeting on 21 April 1913. The Chittagong armoury raid, also known as the Chittagong uprising, was an attempt on 18 April 1930 to raid the armoury of police and auxiliary forces from the Chittagong armoury in the Bengal Presidency of British India (now in Bangladesh) by armed Indian freedom ﬁ ghters led by Surya Sen. During the World War-I (1914-1918), an organisation was founded in Germany, called the Berlin Committee. After 1915, it was renamed the Indian Independence Committee. On April 8, 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt hurled two bombs into the chamber of the Central Legislative Assembly, while it was in session.
questions.explanationHi: सही उत्तर: (A) गदर आंदोलन 20वीं सदी की शुरुआत में भारत में ब्रिटिश शासन को उखाड़ फेंकने के लिए प्रवासी भारतीयों द्वारा आयोजित एक अंतरराष्ट्रीय राजनीतिक आंदोलन था। आंदोलन के जन्म की आधिकारिक तारीख 21 अप्रैल 1913 को एक बैठक मानी गई है। चटगांव शस्त्रागार पर छापा, जिसे चटगांव विद्रोह के रूप में भी जाना जाता है, 18 अप्रैल 1930 को सूर्य सेन के नेतृत्व में सशस्त्र भारतीय स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों द्वारा ब्रिटिश भारत के बंगाल प्रेसीडेंसी (अब बांग्लादेश में) में चटगांव शस्त्रागार से पुलिस और सहायक बलों के शस्त्रागार पर छापा मारने का एक प्रयास था। (1914-1918), जर्मनी में एक संगठन की स्थापना की गई, जिसे बर्लिन समिति कहा जाता है। 1915 के बाद इसका नाम बदलकर भारतीय स्वतंत्रता समिति कर दिया गया। 8 अप्रैल, 1929 को, भगत सिंह और बटुकेश्वर दत्त ने केंद्रीय विधान सभा के कक्ष में दो बम फेंके, जब यह सत्र चल रहा था।

questions.explanationEn: Correct Answer: (C). Ras Bihari Bose was an immigrant Indian living in Japan. On 28-30th March 1942, Bose convened a conference in Tokyo (Japan) to discuss political issues with Indians. Bose decided to establish the Indian Independence League. It was structured during the Bangkok Convention which took place in June, 1942 where Subhash Chandra Bose was invited. During this Conference, Ras Bihari Bose established Indian Independence League. Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement *British Government announced the partition of Bengal on 20 July, 1905. On 7 August 1905, a historic meeting took place at the town hall of Calcutta and the Swadeshi movement was started. The historic Boycott resolution was passed here. After this anti-partition movements started in various parts of Bengal. *On 16 October 1905, the partition formally came into force and Bengal was divided. The day was observed as the 'Mourning day' in the whole Bengal. On the suggestion of Rabindranath Tagore the day was celebrated as ‘Rakhi Diwas’ amongst the people of Bengal. *After its partition, the Bengal was divided into East and West Bengal. East Bengal was merged into Assam, and a new province was formed which included Rajshahi, Chatgaon, Dhaka etc. Dhaka was the headquarter of this province. *Its second part included West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar. *Bengal was divided during the tenure of Lord Curzon (1899-1905). *Sir Andrew Henderson Leith Fraser was an ofﬁ cer of Indian Civil Services. He served as the lieutenant governor of Bengal from 1903-1908. He played an important role in the planning of Bengal Partition. *Rabindra Nath Tagore was a critic of Swadeshi Movement and he emphasised on better relation between the East and West cultures. He believed that the West had committed some mistake in understanding the East, this doesn't mean East do the same with the West. *Krishna Kumar Mitra the editor of ‘Sanjivani’, published a special edition on 13 July 1905, and for the ﬁ rst time suggested that people should boycott British goods, and mourn against the partition and should break all linkages from British ofﬁ cers and ofﬁ ces. All of this should be done as a protest against the partition of Bengal. *A public gathering on 16 July 1905, at district Bagerhat (Division Khulna) supported the suggestion of Krishna Kumar Mitra. *British Government called partition a necessity for the administrative purposes but the real reason was to weaken the growth of Nationalism in Bengal. According to then viceroy Lord Curzon, “Partition was an attempt to strengthen the crown rule and to destroy the centre from which congress party was working and conspiring against the government all over the country.” *Partition of Bengal was the immediate cause of Swadeshi movement. Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai were the main proposers of this idea. They wanted a country wide Swadeshi movement but the moderates were against this. *The Swadeshi Movement that started in Bengal was led by Tilak throughout the country especially at Bombay and Pune. Ajeet Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai led the movement in Punjab and U.P., Sayyed Haider Raja led this movement at Delhi and Chidambaram Pillai led the Swadeshi movement at Madras Presidency. *To organise masses for this movement Ashwini Kumar Dutt founded “Swadesh Bandhav Samiti”. Women played an active role in this movement. However, farmers and Muslims stayed away from Swadeshi and Boycott movement. *Vande Mataram became the title song of Indian National movement during the Swadeshi movement. * British journalist H.W. Nevinson was related to Swadeshi Movement. He travelled for four month across India and he reported for Manchester guardian, Glasgow Herald and Daily Chronicle. Later on, he compiled his reports in a Book ‘The New Spirit in India’. *In the atmosphere of increasing National Movement Avanindra Nath Tagore and his brother Gaganedranath Tagore founded Indian Society of Oriental Arts in 1907 to reconstruct the precious Indian Arts and Culture and to develop new consciousness among the masses. 1. Which of the following occurred last: (a) Annexation Policy (b) Partition of Bengal (c) Permanent Settlement (d) Subsidiary Alliance U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2000 Ans. (b) In the above-mentioned events, the event of Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793. Subsidiary Alliance was a system of the rulers which was introduced by Lord Wellesley in India. The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy purportedly devised by Lord Dalhousie, who was the Governor-General of India in 1848-56. From the above option, the partition of Bengal was the last event announced in July, 1905 by Lord Curzon.

सम्मेलन बुलाया। बोस ने इंडियन इंडिपेंडेंस लीग की स्थापना करने का निर्णय लिया। इसकी संरचना जून, 1942 में हुए बैंकॉक सम्मेलन के दौरान की गई थी जहाँ सुभाष चंद्र बोस को आमंत्रित किया गया था। इस सम्मेलन के दौरान रासबिहारी बोस ने इंडियन इंडिपेंडेंस लीग की स्थापना की। बंगाल का विभाजन और स्वदेशी आंदोलन *ब्रिटिश सरकार ने 20 जुलाई, 1905 को बंगाल के विभाजन की घोषणा की। 7 अगस्त, 1905 को कलकत्ता के टाउन हॉल में एक ऐतिहासिक बैठक हुई और स्वदेशी आंदोलन शुरू किया गया। यहां ऐतिहासिक बहिष्कार प्रस्ताव पारित किया गया. इसके बाद बंगाल के विभिन्न हिस्सों में विभाजन विरोधी आंदोलन शुरू हो गये। *16 अक्टूबर 1905 को, विभाजन औपचारिक रूप से लागू हुआ और बंगाल विभाजित हो गया। यह दिन पूरे बंगाल में 'शोक दिवस' के रूप में मनाया गया। रवीन्द्रनाथ टैगोर के सुझाव पर इस दिन को बंगाल के लोगों के बीच 'राखी दिवस' के रूप में मनाया जाने लगा। *विभाजन के बाद बंगाल को पूर्वी और पश्चिमी बंगाल में विभाजित कर दिया गया। पूर्वी बंगाल को असम में मिला दिया गया और एक नया प्रांत बनाया गया जिसमें राजशाही, चटगाँव, ढाका आदि शामिल थे। ढाका इस प्रांत का मुख्यालय था। *इसके दूसरे भाग में पश्चिम बंगाल, ओडिशा और बिहार शामिल थे। *लॉर्ड कर्जन (1899-1905) के कार्यकाल में बंगाल का विभाजन हुआ। *सर एंड्रयू हेंडरसन लीथ फ़्रेज़र भारतीय सिविल सेवा के एक अधिकारी थे। उन्होंने 1903-1908 तक बंगाल के लेफ्टिनेंट गवर्नर के रूप में कार्य किया। उन्होंने बंगाल विभाजन की योजना में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। *रवीन्द्र नाथ टैगोर स्वदेशी आंदोलन के आलोचक थे और उन्होंने पूर्व और पश्चिम संस्कृतियों के बीच बेहतर संबंध पर जोर दिया था। उनका मानना ​​था कि पश्चिम ने पूर्व को समझने में कुछ ग़लती की है, इसका मतलब यह नहीं कि पूर्व भी पश्चिम के साथ वैसा ही करे. *'संजीवनी' के संपादक कृष्ण कुमार मित्र ने 13 जुलाई 1905 को एक विशेष संस्करण प्रकाशित किया और पहली बार सुझाव दिया कि लोगों को ब्रिटिश वस्तुओं का बहिष्कार करना चाहिए, और विभाजन के खिलाफ शोक मनाना चाहिए और ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों और कार्यालयों से सभी संबंध तोड़ देना चाहिए। यह सब बंगाल विभाजन के विरोध स्वरूप किया जाना चाहिए। *16 जुलाई 1905 को जिला बागेरहाट (डिवीजन खुलना) में एक सार्वजनिक सभा ने कृष्ण कुमार मित्रा के सुझाव का समर्थन किया। *ब्रिटिश सरकार ने विभाजन को प्रशासनिक उद्देश्यों के लिए आवश्यक बताया लेकिन वास्तविक कारण बंगाल में राष्ट्रवाद के विकास को कमजोर करना था। तत्कालीन वायसराय लॉर्ड कर्जन के questions.explanation_en: Correct Answer: (C). Ras Bihari Bose was an immigrant Indian living in Japan. On 28-30th March 1942, Bose convened a conference in Tokyo (Japan) to discuss political issues with Indians. Bose decided to establish the Indian Independence League. It was structured during the Bangkok Convention which took place in June, 1942 where Subhash Chandra Bose was invited. During this Conference, Ras Bihari Bose established Indian Independence League. Partition of Bengal and Swadeshi Movement *British Government announced the partition of Bengal on 20 July, 1905. On 7 August 1905, a historic meeting took place at the town hall of Calcutta and the Swadeshi movement was started. The historic Boycott resolution was passed here. After this anti-partition movements started in various parts of Bengal. *On 16 October 1905, the partition formally came into force and Bengal was divided. The day was observed as the 'Mourning day' in the whole Bengal. On the suggestion of Rabindranath Tagore the day was celebrated as ‘Rakhi Diwas’ amongst the people of Bengal. *After its partition, the Bengal was divided into East and West Bengal. East Bengal was merged into Assam, and a new province was formed which included Rajshahi, Chatgaon, Dhaka etc. Dhaka was the headquarter of this province. *Its second part included West Bengal, Odisha and Bihar. *Bengal was divided during the tenure of Lord Curzon (1899-1905). *Sir Andrew Henderson Leith Fraser was an ofﬁ cer of Indian Civil Services. He served as the lieutenant governor of Bengal from 1903-1908. He played an important role in the planning of Bengal Partition. *Rabindra Nath Tagore was a critic of Swadeshi Movement and he emphasised on better relation between the East and West cultures. He believed that the West had committed some mistake in understanding the East, this doesn't mean East do the same with the West. *Krishna Kumar Mitra the editor of ‘Sanjivani’, published a special edition on 13 July 1905, and for the ﬁ rst time suggested that people should boycott British goods, and mourn against the partition and should break all linkages from British ofﬁ cers and ofﬁ ces. All of this should be done as a protest against the partition of Bengal. *A public gathering on 16 July 1905, at district Bagerhat (Division Khulna) supported the suggestion of Krishna Kumar Mitra. *British Government called partition a necessity for the administrative purposes but the real reason was to weaken the growth of Nationalism in Bengal. According to then viceroy Lord Curzon, “Partition was an attempt to strengthen the crown rule and to destroy the centre from which congress party was working and conspiring against the government all over the country.” *Partition of Bengal was the immediate cause of Swadeshi movement. Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal and Lala Lajpat Rai were the main proposers of this idea. They wanted a country wide Swadeshi movement but the moderates were against this. *The Swadeshi Movement that started in Bengal was led by Tilak throughout the country especially at Bombay and Pune. Ajeet Singh and Lala Lajpat Rai led the movement in Punjab and U.P., Sayyed Haider Raja led this movement at Delhi and Chidambaram Pillai led the Swadeshi movement at Madras Presidency. *To organise masses for this movement Ashwini Kumar Dutt founded “Swadesh Bandhav Samiti”. Women played an active role in this movement. However, farmers and Muslims stayed away from Swadeshi and Boycott movement. *Vande Mataram became the title song of Indian National movement during the Swadeshi movement. * British journalist H.W. Nevinson was related to Swadeshi Movement. He travelled for four month across India and he reported for Manchester guardian, Glasgow Herald and Daily Chronicle. Later on, he compiled his reports in a Book ‘The New Spirit in India’. *In the atmosphere of increasing National Movement Avanindra Nath Tagore and his brother Gaganedranath Tagore founded Indian Society of Oriental Arts in 1907 to reconstruct the precious Indian Arts and Culture and to develop new consciousness among the masses. 1. (b) In the above-mentioned events, the event of Permanent Settlement of Bengal was introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793. Subsidiary Alliance was a system of the rulers which was introduced by Lord Wellesley in India. The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy purportedly devised by Lord Dalhousie, who was the Governor-General of India in 1848-56. From the above option, the partition of Bengal was the last event announced in July, 1905 by Lord Curzon.
